title: Meridian Labs early integration notebook
content:
Quick capture from technical intake + followups (notes to self). Purpose: collect explicit integration constraints and unknowns before next Meridian sync. Heavy shorthand.

Call summary (2025-11-12):
- Attendees: Lena (R), Amir (Meridian infra), Priya (R), Jules (R, solutions eng), Claire (Meridian product).
- Meridian is a diagnostics analytics shop; wants a private deployment (VPC) with occasional on-prem data bursts from partner hospitals.
- Primary use: document summarization + structured extraction from physician notes; throughput spiky (batch uploads nightly, API queries during day).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 180ms for short completion calls (<= 128 tokens). Nightly jobs can accept 2–5s.
- Security: patient PHI, must use customer KMS for keys, auditable request logs, SOC2+HIPAA.

Explicit technical requirements captured:
- Network: must support egress-restricted VPC peering to partner data centers; prefer Private deployment with optional on-prem sync agent.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) + support for envelope encryption on cached KV blobs.
- Audit logs: 1 year retention for all request/response metadata; token redaction for certain fields.
- Model: initially want an open LLM comparable to 13B instruction-tuned model; they asked about quantized 4-bit runtimes to save cost.
- Persistence: KV cache persisted across restarts; nightly snapshot export to S3 (encrypted).
- Rate: daytime interactive peak 400 rps concurrent short calls; nightly batch job 50k docs over 4 hours (bulk inference).
- Isolation: multi-tenant footprint but strict tenant isolation required for their customers; dedicated GPU pool preferred but customers evaluating shared pools with strong isolation controls.

Preliminary sizing guesstimates (for internal budgeting):
- Interactive: target p95 180ms -> need small-batched async path and aggressive prefix caching; estimate 4x a40 equivalence for baseline region for expected concurrency. (very rough).
- Batch: batching + fp16/4-bit quantization recommended; nightly window allows for large batch sizes, request aggregator.

Integration gotchas / red flags observed in call:
- Meridian insists on exact request replayability for audits; our current prefix cache eviction policy must be documented and deterministically reproducible for their compliance team.
- They use custom tokenization pipelines (medical tokens), so model tokenizer mismatch risk — need to surface token counts pre-call and allow upstream tokenization option.
- Network constraints: partner hospitals have strict firewall rules — some endpoints may not allow mutual TLS; offline on-prem agent might be necessary for ingestion pipeline.
- Quantization: while 4-bit reduces cost, Meridian is worried about subtle extraction accuracy regressions (entity extraction). Request A/B eval framework before recommending strong quantization.
- SLAs: want an SLA for p95 latency during peak hours. Hosted SLAs cover this, but Private/Dedicated SLAs will need explicit contract.

Open questions (to resolve before proposal):
- Which exact KMS flows do they need? (bring-your-own-key vs. dedicated HSM). Action: Samir to send Meridian KMS architecture questionnaire (due 2025-11-19).
- Do they require full response storage for 12 months or only metadata + redaction? Claire to confirm with compliance (due 2025-11-18).
- Tokenization: will they accept runtime-side tokenization shim or insist on pre-tokenized payloads? (Priya follow up).
- Are partner hospitals going to allow outbound peering to our VPCs from their networks? Need network contact.

Next steps / action items (owner / ETA):
- Samir: KMS questionnaire + rough HSM options doc -> 2025-11-19.
- Priya: prototype tokenization shim that accepts custom mapping and initial perf numbers -> 2025-11-26.
- Jules: cost and perf sketch for private deployment w/ dedicated GPU pool + expected monthly commit options -> 2025-11-21.
- Lena (me): draft SOW skeleton + compliance checklist (HIPAA mapping) for their legal team -> 2025-11-24.
- Team: run quick internal eval comparing 13B open model fp16 vs 4-bit quantized variant on entity-extraction task using their sample dataset (Jules + Eng Applied ML) -> results due 2025-12-03.

Notes to self (informal):
- Bring up deterministic cache snapshotting in engineering sync — must include metadata mapping from request-id -> cache key.
- Consider exposing "token_count_hint" on API so customers with custom tokenizers can annotate to help routing/billing.
- Could propose an intermediate "hybrid" mode: private control plane + dedicated inference cluster in our managed colo with customer-managed KMS — maybe hits their compliance boxes without full on-prem.

Rough mailbox-friendly summary to send to Claire (draft):
- "Thanks again — we captured the high-level constraints (PHI, VPC, KMS, p95 180ms for short calls, nightly bulk jobs). We're preparing a short SOW + compliance checklist and will follow up with a technical questionnaire on KMS and tokenization. Expect sketches of cost/latency by 11/21 and an initial run comparing fp16 vs 4-bit on your extraction task by 12/03. If helpful we can schedule a short network workshop with your hospital partners to validate peering options."

Attachment ideas for follow up email:
- Proposed SOW skeleton (doc).
- KMS questionnaire (sheet).
- Simple tokenization shim demo + perf numbers (demo video + repo link).
- Sample privacy redaction patterns (pdf).

Misc raw capture (random):
- Claire mentioned existing on-prem agent named "MeridianSync" (ask for tech lead name).
- They have a HIPAA contact: Morgan Blake (morgan.blake@meridianlabs.com) - verify.
- Their infra uses AWS in us-west-2 primarily, with some partner hospitals on prem in us-east-1.

End of notes. Will clean and move into official proposal doc once Samir/Jules prototypes land.
